summary: P.U.L.S.E. is an interactive, predictive space-medicine platform designed to help astronauts self-monitor their health and execute autonomous preventive protocols during long-duration Artemis and Mars missions. Grounded in NASA's 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight and the Natural History of Disease model, P.U.L.S.E. shifts crew healthcare from reactive symptom tracking to subclinical early detection. By combining an interactive anatomical Digital Twin, a 3-Factor Predictive Engine (biometrics, sleep/radiation telemetry, and passive 15-second vocal biomarkers), a Near-Infrared (NIR) optical vein-mapping guide for zero-gravity venipuncture, and a radiation-aware pharmacokinetic auditor, P.U.L.S.E. empowers non-physician astronauts to act before medical emergencies escalate—even under severe Earth communication latency.
details:
THE CHALLENGE & OPERATIONAL GAP

Long-duration missions beyond Low Earth Orbit expose astronauts to NASA's five core spaceflight hazards: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity fields, and hostile closed environments. In deep-space transit or Martian surface operations, round-trip communication delays with Earth Flight Surgeons can exceed 35–44 minutes, rendering real-time telemedicine impossible during acute events. Furthermore, astronauts are rarely physicians, may underreport fatigue to avoid losing extravehicular activity (EVA) privileges, and face physiological fluid shifts that complicate routine blood draws and drug absorption.

HOW P.U.L.S.E. WORKS

P.U.L.S.E. (Physiological Unified Life-Support Evaluator) bridges clinical physiology, operational risk auditing, and aerospace human-factors engineering through five integrated modules:

1. Environment-Aware Telemetry & Latency Protocol: Users switch between orbital stations, lunar bases, interplanetary transit, and planetary rovers. The system dynamically calculates Earth communication latency and automatically toggles an "Autonomous Crew Protocol" mode when high signal delay prevents immediate Flight Surgeon intervention.

2. Interactive Anatomical Digital Twin: Following NASA's human-centered interface guidelines, the core dashboard features an interactive human body divided into four systems (Cardiovascular/Vascular, Metabolic/Immunological, Neurocognitive/Mental, and Musculoskeletal). Color-coded thresholds (Green, Amber, Red), dynamic 7-day trend charts, and plain-language "Why is this check needed today?" cards ensure any crew member understands physiological risks without medical jargon.

3. 3-Factor Subclinical Predictive Engine: Inspired by predictive netcode latency algorithms and the epidemiological Natural History of Disease model (pre-pathogenic, subclinical, and clinical stages), P.U.L.S.E. triggers early preventive alerts when three passive micro-deviations align—even if the astronaut reports feeling fine: (a) resting heart rate or glucose elevation, (b) sleep deficit combined with solar radiation spikes, and (c) acoustic micro-tremors detected via a 15-second daily voice log.

4. Camera-Assisted Optical Diagnostics (NIR Vein Mapper & SANS Screening): Leveraging onboard tablet cameras, P.U.L.S.E. includes a Near-Infrared (NIR) Vascular Projection simulator that maps venous bifurcations onto the skin to assist self-administered blood draws and IV placement in microgravity, alongside an interactive Amsler Grid screening tool for Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS).

5. Actionable Triage, Pharmacokinetic Audit & Gamification: Alerts generate step-by-step preventive checklists paired with a Pharmacokinetic Stability Auditor that verifies medication lot degradation against cumulative space radiation and adjusts dosages for microgravity fluid shifts. A daily preventive streak bar gamifies hydration, exercise, and circadian hygiene adherence.

BENEFITS, EXPECTED IMPACT & CREATIVITY

- Core Benefits: Shifts space healthcare from reactive symptom management to proactive subclinical interception, empowers non-physician crew members with plain-language clinical guidance, and reduces medical risk during communication blackouts or high-latency deep-space missions.

- Expected Impact: Enhances crew autonomy and mission readiness for Artemis lunar surface operations and future Mars transit, while offering direct terrestrial applications for remote clinics, telemedicine in low-connectivity regions, and preventive occupational health monitoring.

- Creative Approach: P.U.L.S.E. uniquely combines gaming latency-prediction concepts with clinical epidemiology (detecting hidden subclinical fatigue via passive vocal biomarkers), optical Near-Infrared vein projection for zero-gravity venipuncture, and radiation-aware pharmaceutical stability auditing in a single unified flight-tablet interface.

REAL-WORLD SCALABILITY & MULTI-CREW DEPLOYMENT

This live MVP demonstrates P.U.L.S.E. using a pre-loaded crew profile (CMDR. VANCE, Mission Ares-IV) so evaluators can test all diagnostic algorithms without physical hardware. In an operational NASA deployment across spacecraft, lunar habitats, or Mars transit vehicles, P.U.L.S.E. functions as standardized flight-tablet software where each crew member logs into an individual profile calibrated to their own pre-flight physiological baselines (resting heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, and vocal acoustics). In production, the platform ingests continuous data streams from wearable biometric sensors, onboard radiation dosimeters, and medical optical cameras, while syncing crew readiness summaries to the Mission Commander and Earth Flight Surgeons.

TOOLS, TECHNOLOGIES & AI DISCLOSURE

- Frontend & Interactive Architecture: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, responsive SVG anatomical modeling, and real-time simulated telemetry state management.

- Hosting & Hardware: Cloud static deployment via Netlify; developed and tested on a MacBook Air using native screen capture and microphone recording for the demonstration video.

- AI Generation Disclosure: Large Language Model / AI assistance (Google Gemini) was utilized to structure the clinical-operational architecture, refine technical documentation, and generate the initial HTML/CSS/JavaScript code for the interactive web prototype.
